correctness.rationale: The beta integral on monomials gives a rising factorial in j divided by (n+2)^{overline k}. Its highest Bernstein coefficient is the falling factorial of n, so selfadjointness and polynomial filtration give the Legendre eigenvalues, with zero on the orthogonal tail. Writing m=n+1, the product gives −m log λ=h_k+2m Σ_{r≤k}(artanh(r/m)−r/m), strictly exceeding h_k on positive finite-rank degrees. At k=1 exponent n fails by n log(1+2/n)<2; lower exponents, including M_n^0=I, fail there too. For k≤m/2 the cubic remainder bound gives an error at most (2/9)m^(−2)h_k²e^(−h_k); for k>m/2 including k>n, m<2k≤2h_k gives the asserted constant-4 bound from e^(−h_k). The fixed-degree cubic term is h_k²/(6m²). The displayed diagonal summable majorant gives trace convergence and hence the operator norm conclusion (maximum at h=2). For a fixed c, the remaining exponent shift d=c−1 changes the eigenvalue power by first-order −d h_k e^(−h_k)/m. The power difference at k≤m/2 is dominated after scaling by C_d h_k e^(−h_k/2) using −log λ≤C h_k/m and m−|d|≥m/2; the tail k>m/2 obeys the same type of majorant using m<2k. Replacing scale m by n is asymptotically immaterial. The claimed trace and operator constants agree with independent decimal evaluation.
